problems.description: app.py contains a class not following PascalCase naming (per convention scan; violates project snake_case/PascalCase convention)
test_app.py defines module-level constants in lowercase rather than UPPER_CASE

Rewrites the existing Blueprint/JWT-modular layout into a single flat module (app-level routes, one DB table), abandoning the established Blueprint and auth-decorator pattern; acceptable for a greenfield single-file app but reduces extensibility for subsequent story sessions
Cognitive complexity increased by +11 in a small app, indicating nested conditionals/handlers that could be decomposed into helper functions

strengths: SonarQube reports zero new bugs, zero smells, and zero duplication — clean, coherent rewrite
Uses timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) instead of the legacy datetime.utcnow()
Correct HTTP semantics (201 on create, 400 on missing title) with input validation
Enables PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON and uses timezone-aware created_at timestamps
Net line reduction (+238/-209) keeps the module compact and focused
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, bug-free greenfield rewrite of a Flask seed into a task API, scoring 0.82 on conventions and 0.7 on architecture — penalized for two measured style violations and for discarding the existing Blueprint-based modular pattern in favor of a flat single module.

problems.description: Schema is defined twice for owner_id: CREATE TABLE already includes owner_id but a separate ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN migration is also run inside init_db(), a redundant/duplicate definition that risks drift between the two.
SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-in-production' value; acceptable for a story experiment app but would be a real risk if this code were deployed without setting the env var.
request.user_id is set on the Flask request proxy instead of the idiomatic flask.g; works via LocalProxy forwarding but diverges from standard Flask patterns for per-request state.
test_app.py introduces module-level constants that are not UPPER_CASE, matching the measured convention violation.

strengths: Passwords hashed with werkzeug generate_password_hash/check_password_hash — no plaintext storage.
JWT tokens carry exp and iat and handle ExpiredSignatureError/InvalidTokenError gracefully.
All task endpoints are auth-protected and every query is scoped with owner_id, preventing cross-user access (IDOR).
require_auth uses functools.wraps to preserve function metadata.
Respects the existing single-file Flask app structure and extends the existing test fixtures rather than restructuring.
Measurement shows zero new bugs, reduced smells (-3), and no duplications.
commit_reviews.summary: Clean, well-scoped auth + ownership feature that fits the existing app architecture and reduces smells, with minor debt from the redundant dual schema definition and a dev SECRET_KEY fallback; note that the app.py PascalCase violation reported by the measurement appears pre-existing since this diff adds no classes, while the test_app.py constant-naming violation is introduced here.

compounding_issues: Session 1 wholesale-rewrote the seed, discarding its working auth stack (register/login, token validation, Blueprints) and shipping a bare single-user task CRUD API; session 2 then had to rebuild auth from scratch rather than extending inherited code
The seed's modular Blueprint layout was flattened into a single monolith app.py, a structure session 2 inherited and grew rather than refactoring

init_db() contains a redundant migration path: the tasks table is created WITH owner_id in the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and then an ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN owner_id is attempted in a try/except, leaving two parallel schema paths and an ad-hoc migration approach
Hardcoded dev SECRET_KEY fallback and 24h JWT with no refresh mechanism linger as debt for any later session
key_decisions: Session 1 chose greenfield reinterpretation: drop the seed's multi-user auth API and build a minimal tasks CRUD app (only 3 of the original endpoints retained, renamed auth_api.db to tasks.db)
Session 2 adopted JWT (PyJWT, HS256) with werkzeug generate_password_hash/check_password_hash, replacing the seed's static-salt SHA-256 scheme and its own session-1 no-auth state
Session 2 added per-user tenancy via tasks.owner_id FK and scoped every task query (create/list/get/update) to request.user_id, enforcing user isolation at the API layer
Kept a single-file Flask app throughout rather than restoring the seed's Blueprint structure, prioritizing minimal diff size over modularity
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the two sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, minimal, fully test-covered task CRUD API (18 tests passing) but regressed scope by dropping all authentication. Session 2 was a genuine feature addition that built directly on session 1's task model, layering in JWT auth, proper password hashing, and per-user task isolation, with the test suite more than doubling to 39 tests and all passing at the final commit. The code grew more complex yet remained stylistically consistent and green, so the overall arc is clearly upward, marred only by the seed's discarded auth work being re-derived from scratch.
story_review.summary: A coherent two-session arc — minimal task CRUD then JWT-authenticated multi-user isolation, all tests passing — that built naturally on itself, though session 1's throwaway rewrite of the seed's auth forced session 2 to reinvent rather than extend.
